messages:
kim: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands: can someone clarify release cadence for the next quarter and the oncall expectations during canaries? Also, what's our minimum quality bar to kick off a canary?

maria_gonzalez: short answer: monthly feature releases with a 10-14 day freeze before ship week; ad-hoc hotfixes for incidents.

dave_sre: Oncall during canary: the "canary_owner" listed in the rollout PR owns alerts for the canary window and must post a start message in #eng-oncall. If SLA-sensitive routes are involved, CC SRE lead before promoting past 20% traffic.

elaine_cto: Canary windows usually 12-72h depending on risk. Promote once metrics are stable for the agreed window.

kim: which metrics exactly are required to be green?

maria_gonzalez: primary gates: P95 latency <= 1.2x baseline, error-rate delta < 0.1% absolute on service errors, and no customer-facing regressions from our smoke/regression suites. CI smoke must pass.

product-ops: do we have a freeze checklist engineers can follow?

release-bot: Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/release-process (freeze checklist + PR template) :link:

maria_gonzalez: checklist highlights: release notes, canary traffic plan, rollback doc, perf smoke, QA subset green, canary_owner assigned and pinged.

kim: handling flakies post-canary start?

dave_sre: If flaky tests affect release signals: pause promotion, consider rollback, create high-pri ticket, quarantine test in CI. Aim to triage within 4-6h.

elaine_cto: For Dedicated/SLA routes, engineering target is <10% P99 regression. Legal/ops still finalizing contract wording.

maria_gonzalez: I'll run a 30min office hour tomorrow 10am PT to walk teams through the PR template and checklist.

kim: thanks — i'll post a short summary in docs and link the PR snippet.

product-ops: action items: add PR snippet to template, publish freeze checklist, schedule canary-owner training.

release-bot: Reminder: next oncall rotation starts 1930200000.
